decision: Follow the seven-step H2b switch with model tests first and old proofs deleted last.
why: The switch changes durable history and must preserve every acknowledged edit.
result: plan recorded; no product reader moved

decision: Allow historical transition aliases and refuse surplus recorded resources.
why: The lead requires both re-check findings fixed before the session model uses installs.
result: two named regressions red before fix

decision: Keep exact historical transition evidence; reject resource surplus before issuing an install token.
why: Sibling installs must not be vetoed by historical approvals, and accepted saves must preserve combined identity.
result: Both regressions fail before; 88 owner tests and 1178 Core/Project tests pass, 6 ignored; clippy, fmt and slow lint pass.

decision: Use one compact codec and semantic validator with native and in-memory object sources.
why: Portable fault streams must test the stored owner format; Save As and rescue copy the reachable graph to an independent destination and retire the source.
result: Implementation written; first compile queued on the shared Cargo lock; no product caller switched.

decision: Stop the product switch at the Task-to-Candidate merge-budget mismatch.
why: Decision 6 requires the admitted delta to fit its merge path; 2000 accepted task operations encode to 95000 bytes, above Candidate 65536.
result: Candidate returns History(StepTooLarge); ADMITTED_TASK_DELTA_MUST_FIT_CANDIDATE_MERGE_PATH fails; profiles unchanged.

decision: Keep the complete generated corpus and canonical state checks in portable and native-store tests.
why: The new executor, owner and compact codec must preserve acknowledged transitions and reachable resources through recovery before product callers move.
result: 1182 Core/Project tests pass, 7 ignored; long corpus 65536 random attempts plus 128 primer transitions passes in 291.12 s; clippy, fmt and slow lint pass; all 64 seeds checked exactly once.

decision: Split the long portable corpus into sixteen four-seed tests, each retaining four Rust workers.
why: The Windows 600-second process limit is unchanged; each manifest unit now contains 4096 attempts and failures name the seed and attempt.
result: 16 units pass in 18.347-27.264 s each; all 64 seeds and 65536 attempts plus 128 primer transitions retained; original coverage totals unchanged; 1182 Core/Project tests pass, 22 ignored; clippy, fmt and slow lint pass.

decision: Stop before changing product profiles or moving callers at the authorized 768 MiB boundary.
why: With the existing four-slot caches, measured component minima require at least 796.763 MiB for eight Task leases, one Ordinary lease and shared workspace; this excludes every Candidate and capture.
result: Size probe exits zero: 20000 clips 3179988 encoded / 4800848 live, 7200848 live after one four-track cut; 2000 removals 850911 encoded / 20433822 decoded, merged decoded 19730174. Candidate-only measured charging cannot remove this floor; no profiles or product callers changed; checkpoint 1 and shipping builds not reached.

decision: Isolate every slow Project case while keeping its fast tier in one batch.
why: The previous test split still ran all sixteen in one CI process; give each an independent 600-second process and provisional Windows weight at five times rounded-up local time.
result: Named assertion red before; 26 shard and 52 slow-test self-tests pass; eight-shard predicted spreads 59.583 s Linux and 56.957 s Windows; 1182 Core/Project tests pass, 22 ignored; clippy, fmt and manifest lint pass.

decision: Stop before implementing creation sizing because the current snapshot leases and live RunCandidate lifecycle require additional ownership changes.
why: An Ordinary Core plus its independent full capture needs 208 MiB inside the specified 128 MiB pool; the RunCandidate is persisted before any frozen delta exists. Original candidate charges and baseline spare capacity are absent from stored records.
result: Portable probe passes: initial charges 48/512 versus 3040/10592 converge to identical 864-byte records; baseline live sizes 440 versus 1966536 converge to identical 635-byte records; capture with the specified 24 MiB free headroom is refused atomically. No product profiles, records or callers changed.

decision: Fix Ordinary at 104 MiB; creation-size Task and both Candidate kinds with a 2 MiB document floor, 3 MiB owner allowance, one Task cache anchor and no Candidate cache anchors.
why: The measured 2000 four-track removals need 1966704 live bytes; eight 5000-clip tasks plus a capture fit 400 MiB.
result: Change the floor or anchor count only with the merge-fit, task-room and product performance gates.

decision: Leave room for one full largest-task capture when admitting a Task Core.
why: A pool full of tasks must still let one task checkpoint and release its lease; snapshot admissions use that reserved headroom.
result: Measured-size snapshot leases would remove this headroom requirement.

decision: Give GUI and writer independent process pools; use an independent cold verification reader pool.
why: The product has one pool per process; treating two processes and an oracle as a single process falsely counts their simultaneous ordinary leases together.
result: A future in-process writer must share the GUI pool and rerun the peak assertion.

decision: Persist creation kind, original baseline live and owner charges and initial staging batch charge; hash all fields in snapshot identity.
why: Current records cannot recover either initial delta charge or original spare capacity after edits. No missing-descriptor reader is added.
result: Leases that grow with use are a later lifecycle design.

decision: Size Ordinary for two live tabs plus a Save: 312 MiB, with one capture kept free at live-Core admission.
why: App::new_project keeps the first ProjectSession Core and pushes the second, so its Save needs three leases; a refused new tab leaves both live states intact.
result: The one-project model still asserts peak <=2; a third live tab needs a later measured-size lease design.

decision: Use the full 72 MiB maximum for each Candidate and a 168 MiB shared workspace: 312+400+144+168=1024 MiB.
why: The plain fixture's 60.709 MiB estimate excludes richer baseline lineage; all admitted descriptors must fit a fresh merge destination. Ordinary ripple scratch is (7*8+3*32+headers)*1.1 <168 MiB.
result: Change only if actual product-path counters or replay peak measurements invalidate the arithmetic.

decision: Charge occurrence insertion and ancestry-vector growth separately instead of doubling the entire existing lineage map.
why: The 20000-clip boundary query refused with 17.7 MiB of lineage inside its 32 MiB owner allowance. Existing map nodes do not double on insertion; only the ancestry Vec may do so.
result: WHAT_CAN_BE_SAVED_CAN_BE_OPENED passed; the subsequent boundary query exposed Capacity(lineage). Preserve the existing node and payload overcharges and test every returned boundary.

decision: Charge N retained observation slots and one transient kernel slot, plus geometric command/fate containers; record kernel scratch separately.
why: The 2000-removal qualification was refused at cut 1948 because every transient vector was charged as retained; an independent actual-capacity test pins the container charge.
result: A later observation container change must update the capacity assertion and admission proof.

decision: Admit the maximum of real and canonical replay buffer capacity per field; pad the initial baseline once and canonicalise only at installation.
why: Wire Vec capacities can differ from the originating process. The same document limit must cover both, without storing allocation topology or copying documents on warm commands.
result: The source, saved-open and fresh-merge regression pins a long split stream with spare baseline capacity.

decision: Use a boundary holder's full retained lease for its document and lineage; exclude the unused operation/cache allowance from the lineage restriction.
why: A boundary owns no operation stacks. The 2000-removal query also exposed Clip inline bytes counted both in ancestry Vec slots and its heap charge.
result: Measured-size query leases could reduce accounting later; every result must still fit its admitted lease.

decision: Cap the live aggregate decode forecast at the existing 64 MiB structural decoder ceiling.
why: A larger workspace must not allow a live body which the unchanged decoder will refuse after Save.
result: Changing the decoder ceiling requires a separate memory calculation; it is not raised here.

decision: Use max(2*baseline live+512 KiB,baseline live+2 MiB), capped at 8 MiB.
why: The real Ordinary-to-Task constructor path sees replay-padded baseline capacities; the previous floor gave seven rather than eight Task slots at 5000 clips.
result: The named constructor assertion is red before and green after; required 2000-removal room is requalified on the unchanged fixture.

decision: Reserve geometric wire capacity as well as actual capacity for input-reference and approval-target vectors.
why: A length-one vec and its cold JSON decode have different capacities; a full manifest-context Task could be saved but not reopened.
result: ADMITTED_MANIFEST_CONTEXT_HISTORY_REOPENS is red before and green after; no normalising copy or limit increase.

decision: Put the product actor over OwnerHistory in the Project crate; keep the pure executor and operation DTOs in Core.
why: Core cannot own Project records without reversing the dependency; one monomorphic actor avoids a generic owner callback framework.
result: The actor and its leased readers compile beside the old product actor; product callers move in the integration commit. Retirement acknowledges actual document and lease destruction.

decision: Hash the live canonical owner view when freezing instead of creating a retained capture.
why: A full immutable capture is charged separately; a constant-size attachment cut need not retain documents or seed maps.
result: Capture and live identities agree after folds; warm commands take no owner hash.

decision: Apply the immutable creation owner allowance and structural decoder ceiling to transition approvals.
why: The old role-maximum check could spend beyond the smaller creation lease after Do metadata had used its room.
result: Named assertion fails before and passes after; refusal preserves the complete state.

decision: Use one independently leased trusted working state and publish its borrowed prospective destination view before replacing the live state.
why: A staging candidate is creation-sized, while the existing LiveCandidate retains its full immutable descriptor. Capturing a third history merely to encode the future record would exceed the two-candidate envelope.
result: No extra retained capture, lease growth or snapshot-install epoch. The old state is dropped under the admitted working holder before acknowledgement; the live lease stays fixed.

decision: Construct private previews only from validated live History, never from raw Record.
why: A raw record must pass semantic replay; a process-admitted prefix can share immutable documents and recorded peaks.
result: The untrusted prevalidated shortcut is unreachable by type. The preview keeps keys, both stacks and the epoch.

decision: Give the new accepted-command codec a 2 MiB pending-byte window and retain the 64-command count.
why: An admitted 1041035-byte source message failed the old 262144-byte window. Ruling 5 requires that the fresh destination transport also fits an admitted source step and its context.
result: The relation is compile-time asserted and the maximal source witness is permanent. Producer retention will hold encoded messages inside the existing Ordinary envelope, not add a full history lease.

decision: Run the permanent session corpus through the production normalised actions, chained messages and bounded receipt state.
why: A separate model implementation of the agreement would not exercise the code being switched. Keep an oracle-only archive of receipts observed in published roots, rather than an unbounded product receipt list.
result: 1216 Core/Project tests pass, 24 ignored; all 64 seeds and 65536 attempts pass in 16 release units (13.95 s). Ordinary peak remains two. Core-only comparison mutation is red at INSTALL_EQUALITY_USES_COMBINED_SNAPSHOT_IDENTITY and reverted.
